evals.expected_output: Reads the diff and the repo's enforced convention, then makes one commit with a gitmoji message and reports it
expectations: Runs git status and git diff before writing a message
Looks for the repo's commit-msg check (commitlint config or lefthook commit-msg) before choosing a type
Uses a type the repo's check accepts, in the emoji type(scope): subject format
Stages by explicit path, never git add . or git add -A
For a single-commit change, commits without asking and then shows the message and hash
Adds no AI attribution trailer

evals.prompt: I changed 8 files across auth and billing, commit everything as one commit
evals.expected_output: Identifies mixed scopes, proposes splitting into 2+ commits, does not blindly commit everything together
expectations: Detects that files span multiple unrelated scopes (auth and billing)
Recommends splitting into at least 2 commits rather than one
Proposes separate commit messages for each group
Explains the reason for splitting (mixed scope)
Asks for confirmation of the multi-commit plan and waits before committing

evals.prompt: setup lefthook and commit message linting for my new project
evals.expected_output: Reads hooks-and-tools.md, picks the variant from whether the repo has a package.json, and produces the matching lefthook.yml and commit-msg check
expectations: Reads the hooks-and-tools.md reference file before responding
Checks whether the repo has a package.json before choosing a variant
With a package.json: provides commitlint.config.mjs with the emoji type list and the bun install commands
Without a package.json: provides the grep-based commit-msg hook and adds no JS dependency
Provides a lefthook.yml covering pre-commit, commit-msg, and pre-push

evals.prompt: I accidentally committed an API key in the last commit, what do I do
evals.expected_output: Reads security.md, guides through key rotation first then history cleanup
expectations: Reads the security.md reference file before responding
Instructs to rotate/revoke the key immediately as the first step
Explains how to remove the secret from git history (BFG or git-filter-repo)
Mentions that force push is required and warns about coordination with collaborators
Does not suggest git commit --amend as a safe fix (amend only rewrites local unpushed history)

evals.prompt: I have one file with two unrelated fixes — a CSS typo and a JS bug. How should I commit this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends git add -p to stage hunks separately, proposes two commit messages
expectations: Recommends using git add -p (patch mode) for partial file staging
Proposes two separate commit messages with appropriate types (style + fix)
Does not suggest committing the file as a whole in one commit
Shows the correct git add -p command syntax

evals.prompt: check if my branch has any secrets before I push
evals.expected_output: Reads security.md, provides gitleaks command and manual grep pattern for staged/history scanning
expectations: Reads the security.md reference file
Provides a gitleaks command appropriate for scanning (git history or staged)
Includes the manual grep pattern as a fallback
Clarifies the difference between scanning staged-only vs full history

evals.expected_output: In a repo whose commit-msg hook accepts only standard Conventional Commit types, commits a config-file change as chore rather than configs
expectations: Reads the commit-msg hook's accepted type list before choosing a type
Does not use the configs type when the hook's type list lacks it
Uses the nearest accepted type (chore) and keeps the leading emoji
The commit lands on the first attempt, with no hook rejection

evals.prompt: commit everything, split it up properly
evals.expected_output: When a commit in a multi-commit plan is rejected by a hook, fixes and retries that commit before staging the next group
expectations: After each git commit, verifies it landed (git log -1 shows the header just written)
On a hook rejection, fixes the cause and retries the same commit
Does not stage the next group while the rejected commit's files are still staged
Final history has one commit per planned group, with no group merged into another
